content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wings are pieces of a chicken's wing, usually deep‑fried or grilled. In fast‑food they are served breaded and often accompanied by sauces such as barbecue, hot, or honey‑mustard. Wings are popular for their crispy coating and juicy meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings became a staple in the US in the early 20th century when bars started selling “barbecue wings”.
The classic American style is “Buffalo wings”, tossed in a spicy butter‑based sauce.
In Japan a version called “yakitori” marinates wings in soy sauce and grills them.
Wings are a common contest food; the 10‑minute eating record exceeds 200 pieces.
National Chicken Wing Day is celebrated on July 29 in the United States.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken wings provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Wings supply iron, zinc, and phosphorus, which are essential for blood health and bones.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Makes them suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Fried wings can contain up to 300 kcal and 20 g of fat per 100 g, which may be excessive if over‑consumed.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Salty and sauce‑laden versions often have high sodium, which can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Cooking contaminants
items.content: Very high frying temperatures can produce acrylamide and other potentially harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wings are served hot, usually in portion boxes. They are eaten with the hands, pulling the meat off the bone. Dip them in sauces like barbecue, ranch, blue cheese, or hot chili. For a healthier option, bake them without breading.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked fried wings keep in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days in an airtight container. Frozen raw wings store up to 6 months at –18 °C. Reheat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before eating.
